lens: Brand guardian and truth: fit with Naira's brand, voice and the owner's documented likes and dislikes; whether every claim holds up against research/roster.json and the listing text (price, stock, tags, mm/cm, stone and finish words, alt text); cultural accuracy; taste risks (kitsch, clutter, near-black or beige grounds, stuck-on florals); legal exposure; consistency; wordmark and type rules. All 12 posts of each proposal were read in full. Prices and stock were checked by script against roster.json: every quoted price matches, no hero is pre-order, every piece has 18 or more in stock, and the lowest variant is 12 (Ruby bracelet and huggies). Material and size facts were checked against src/data/jewellerySnapshot.ts and the roster image alt text.

scores.criteria: brand fit 9: tells the true couture-house story through an Indian institution every buyer knows; the real wordmark sits on the two signboard bookends (P1, P12); Velista, Cormorant and Jost; the brand's own palette families; deck tulips used as a fabric print, never stuck on. | owner-taste fit 8: everyday wit with restraint (P2 moon always late, P4 send this to your brother, P5 is it gold, P6 kandil, P11 tulsi), three violet grounds, night grounds, one piece per frame, and the kind of honesty she loved ('is it real gold? NO.'). Against it: P9's apricot tint #F7E1D2 is close to the beige she rejects, P2's plum #3B2330 reads near-black at 36%, and there are 3 AI textile textures. | truthfulness 7: the best honesty devices of the four (P5 'SOLID GOLD?: no.'; P5 s4 'listed as waterproof. we'd still take them off to swim.'; GREEN rather than emerald everywhere), and no other water claims. But P2 is wrong: the Cushion Halo Ring's centre is an 8 mm ROUND brilliant (only the halo is cushion-shaped), and the listing says fixed US 7, so 'Sizes are on its page' misleads. P8 calls the 40 cm marquise chain a 'choker'. P4 says 'gold-tone knots' where the listing says 'stacked gold rings'. P10's bracelet pavé link conflicts with the listing text. | cultural accuracy 9: मॅचिंग सेंटर uses the chandra, as Marathi shop boards spell it. Aai, Vahini, Paithani for Padwa, Bhaubeej, the akash kandil kept up through Kartik (softened to 'in a lot of homes'), and Tulsi as the season's first wedding with no product near the plant are all right. | voice/caption quality 9: 'the moon is always late. so we matched a ring to it.', 'he has never once guessed right.', 'the rest of us are guests.'; hooks of 43-88 characters; offer line in 5 of 12 captions; no dashes or exclamation marks. | premium execution risk 7: one swatch, one tag and one piece per tile is buildable. The danger is the humble institution done cheaply (painted signboard, synthetic-looking silk, Paithani or sequin textures). | restraint vs clutter 8: P11 carries no product at all; the tag is the only recurring device; only P8's index runs dense. | legal risk 7: P2's stone and sizing misstatement is a misleading product claim until fixed. The WhatsApp promise ('three matches with photographs', in five posts) is an operational commitment the owner must confirm. | consistency 9: SHADE N° equals the post number, the tag hangs on nine covers, the signboards bookend the long diagonal and the checkerboard carries up from LAC/BONE. | wordmark/type rules 8: the wordmark appears only on the signboards (box-lid photos count as the frame's one); three faces plus Tiro Devanagari; no Kalam. The 26 px blush flower on the tags bends the 6-15% ghost rule, so it is the owner's call.
best_posts: P5 'IS IT GOLD?': Dhanteras answered with an order slip ('18k gold tone plated · SOLID GOLD?: no.'), a tape at 25 mm, and 'we'd still take them off to swim'. The most on-brand honesty in any option.
P4 'SEND THIS TO YOUR BROTHER. he has never once guessed right.': loving sibling wit built to be forwarded; Duo Link Bracelet ₹999, 20 in stock.
P6 'THE KANDIL STAYS UP ALL MONTH. so can this.': the pastel akash kandil in Prism's own colours on bottle green; a Diwali tile with no red-and-gold cliché.
P11 Tulsi Vivah, 'the first wedding of the season is the tulsi's. the rest of us are guests.': respectful, specific, product-free breathing tile.
P12 'GUEST ORDERS UNDERTAKEN.': the vernacular board line reworked for the guest, with the ruby set and a bill at list prices and no discount on the art.
weakest_posts: P2 as written: wrong stone cut, wrong sizing claim, and a fixed-size ring offered as a Karwa Chauth surprise gift; plum #3B2330 reads near-black.
P8 Five functions: five pieces in 7 slides, the 'choker' error, an AI sequin swatch, and a mehendi cone drawn with paste: the densest tile in an otherwise quiet set.
P9 '36 CM.': the apricot-tint ground risks the beige read, and it is the third post selling the baguette set in four weeks (P1, P9, P12).
P1 key art: a 5-slide explainer plus a five-script board slide; the first post after 76 days leads on a service promise that is not yet confirmed.
fatal_or_must_fix: P2 Cushion Halo Ring: rewrite to 'a round brilliant cubic zirconia, about 8 mm, in a cushion-shaped pavé halo' and drop 'Sizes are on its page'. The listing says 'US 7, fixed size, not adjustable' while the roster alt text says 'adjustable band split at the back', so fix the listing. Better for a Karwa Chauth gift: swap to an adjustable or size-free piece (Verdant Eternity Band, rhodium, adjusts US 6-8, 60 in stock; or Silk Mesh Cuff, 40 in stock).
P8 s6: 'a marquise choker over a marquise lariat' is wrong. Listing: a 40 cm chain with one marquise cubic zirconia plus a Y-lariat with 5 mm marquise stations.
P4: 'joined by small gold-tone knots' becomes the listing's 'small stacked gold rings', unless the macro clearly shows a knot.

P10 (and P8 index): confirm the Bold Nocturne Bracelet has a pavé link before saying 'each with one pavé link'. The listing text says 'thick flat curb link' while the AI-styled alt text shows a pavé link; fix the listing.

Owner must confirm the WhatsApp 'send a photo, get three matches with photographs' service (P1, P3, P8, P11, P12) can be staffed Mon-Sat 10-7 through the festive weeks. If not, use the site's exact gifting line.
P9 ground: move from #F7E1D2 to the Apricot edition ground #F0C9AC or to blush, so it cannot read as sand or beige. P2 ground: lift #3B2330 toward plum #4E3C66 so it does not read black.
Native readers for मॅचिंग सेंटर, मैचिंग सेंटर and the Kannada, Tamil and Telugu boards on P1 s4; drop any board that cannot be verified.
graftable_ideas: P5's order-slip honesty ('IS IT GOLD? … SOLID GOLD?: no.') as the Dhanteras answer in any option.
P5 s4's water line ('listed as waterproof. we'd still take them off to swim.') as the house's only way to mention water.
The GREEN-not-emerald labelling on every Edition Two colour.
The SHADE N° tag: one small, repeatable lockup that never fights the piece.
P11's product-free Tulsi Vivah greeting as a breathing tile.
P4's forwardable 'send this to your brother' format for Bhai Dooj.

scores.criteria: brand fit 9: the purest expression of the true story. A couture house says the thread decides the metal; outfits are made to measure in Nashik and the jewellery is never called handmade. The stitched label puts the wordmark in the same place on every cover. | owner-taste fit 7: lilac (P8), LAC oxblood, bottle green and plum nights, one pressed deck sprig, exact mm and cm, no black or sand. But there is less of the Indian-object wit she scores highest (only chalni and the card party), and four pale paper covers (P1, P3, P9, P11) risk the 'accurate and dead' read. | truthfulness 8: every mm and cm matches the listings (Silk Mesh 15/19 mm withheld; Toggle clasp deliberately not described; 36 cm sourced from the roster alt text), and there are zero water, tarnish or hypoallergenic claims. Slips: alt text says 'a fine gold bracelet' (P4) and 'small gold flower studs' / 'gold pavé link drop earrings' (P5); P1 s2 says 'wear the gold.'; P3 s2 says 'emerald cubic zirconia'; P10 s5 sets 'EMERALD.' as a Velista headline. | cultural accuracy 9: chalni on Karwa Chauth with no fasting or husband framing (P2); Ganga-Jamuni for two-tone (P1 s4); the Diwali card party (P4, P5); the head covered at a gurudwara (P11); haldi, mehendi, sangeet, shaadi and reception in the right order (P12). A low-risk register. | voice/caption quality 8: crisp, saveable house rules ('THE THREAD DECIDES THE METAL.', 'MEASUREMENTS: NOT NEEDED.', 'It has never once said a necklace was too short.'). Captions run long and instructive, and the offer line is in 8 of 12. | premium execution risk 6: the scrapbook stack (ruled paper, pinked swatches, gradient glass-head pins, Kalam notes, pencil arrows, glassine strip, label) can tip into crafty Pinterest. Kalam stands in for the founder's hand. The exhibition cut-outs are low-res, and three on-model plates are Higgsfield generations (P3, P7, P10). | restraint vs clutter 6: P1's cover carries 2 swatches, 2 cut-outs, 4 pins, 2 notes, an aside, a headline, a folio and the label. P12 (top-left, the first thing ad traffic sees) carries 5 figures, 5 pieces at 100 px, 5 tags, pins and a note. | legal risk 9: no claim beyond the listing; the couture shoots are the house's own (confirm model releases); nothing borrowed. | consistency 9: the label sits in one place, the pages are numbered, and every cross-reference agrees (P5 to P1, P7 to P3, P12 to pages 1/3/8/9/11). | wordmark/type rules 7: the wordmark appears once, inside the label, except on P4, where the box-lid print plus the label put two marks in one frame. Kalam is a fourth face. Velista glyph limits are respected.
best_posts: P2 'CHALNI, FOR THE WRIST.': Karwa Chauth as one object (an embroidery hoop as the sieve and the moon) on the exact LAC oxblood; Silk Mesh Cuff with no size risk.
P3 'FIRST THE NECKLINE. then the necklace.': the most saveable guide in any option; real lengths; pushes the necklace category (Baguette Tennis Necklace 70 in stock, 0 sold; Toggle 79).
P6 '25 MM.': a quiet Diwali-day tile, the tape drawn at true scale, 'Shubh Deepavali' kept in the caption.
P11 'NOTHING FOR THE NET TO CATCH.': a real Indian-wedding problem (net dupattas snag drops) solved with huggies.
P8 'THE THIMBLE COMES OFF AT SIX.': lilac, one tool, one adjustable ring, 'green cubic zirconia, not emerald. We'd rather tell you.'
weakest_posts: P12 Look List cover: the busiest tile in the set sits top-left; five full couture figures with faces; pieces at 100 px will not read at 36%.
P4 reel 'MEASUREMENTS: NOT NEEDED.': two wordmarks in one frame (box lid plus label); the order-slip conceit is the weakest joke.
P9 'THE SLEEVE DECIDES THE WRIST.': five products, the third pale pattern-paper tile, guide fatigue by week three.
P1 cover: a dense scrapbook opener after 76 days of silence.
fatal_or_must_fix: P4: the box-lid wordmark plus the label wordmark make two marks in one frame (a judged violation in Up Close). Drop the label on this reel or turn the box so the lid print is not visible.

P12 cover: crop the five couture figures below the chin, or cut to three larger figures. Faces on product tiles are on the owner's dislike list, and the pinned pieces must be large enough to read in the grid.
Alt text uses bare 'gold': P4 'a fine gold bracelet', P5 'small gold flower studs' and 'gold pavé link drop earrings'. Change to 'gold-tone'.
Copy: P1 s2 'wear the gold.' becomes 'wear gold tone.'; P3 s2 'emerald cubic zirconia' becomes 'green cubic zirconia'; P10 s5 'RUBY, CRYSTAL, EMERALD.' becomes 'RUBY, CRYSTAL, GREEN.'
Kalam needs the owner's sign-off. If a font is used, it must never be presented as Vandana's handwriting; a real graphite scan is the honest version.
Clutter cap: hold the promised one swatch or one tool per cover and at most three notes; cut pins that hold nothing.
graftable_ideas: P1 'the thread decides the metal' as the Edition Two metal-choice explainer (gold tone vs rhodium vs two-tone).
P3's neckline croquis with 36/40/45/50 cm arcs: a guide any option can carry.
P6's tape drawn at true scale with 'drawn at the same scale' stated on the image.
P11's dupatta-snag guide.
The stitched woven house label as a consistent lockup that keeps the wordmark on every cover.
P2's Silk Mesh Cuff as a safer, size-free Karwa Chauth piece (it fixes Matching Centre P2).

scores.proposal: proposal-indian-pop.json · MANGAL: the Tuesday gold season
scores.criteria: brand fit 7: built from Naira inks, Velista, Cormorant, Jost and the bag's tulips, with the owner's own spine line. But two-ink misregistration, cream keylines, the sunburst and a nine-script seal push the house into festive-pop far from its quiet premium shipped work. | owner-taste fit 7: it carries most of her top-scored wit (locker gold P3, dabba P6, missed call P8, good box P9) and lilac and plum nights. Against it: a full marigold ground on the opener P1 and coral on P7; a tulip-cluster bracket applied to ten tiles (the stuck-on-floral risk); seals laid over her clean approved plates (P5, P11); kaju katli two posts running (P6 drawn, P7 photo). | truthfulness 8: zero water claims, listing-exact facts, 'ruby-red cubic zirconia', 'mint, not emerald', and honest after-the-day delivery lines (P2, P7). Flags: P3's cover sets 'NOT LOCKER GOLD. TUESDAY GOLD.' over 'WOVEN GOLD HOOPS · ₹1,299' with no tone bracket on that slide; P6 s2 'ONE ROW OF RUBY.' says nothing about cubic zirconia; four AI-generated plates (P3 mirror photo, P5 rangoli, P7 kaju katli, P11 invitation) need checking against the listings. | cultural accuracy 7: the rituals are right: chalni, then his face, then water (P2); aukshan on Padwa and the pre-dawn oil bath (P4); faral dabba (P6); shagun ending in one (P7); antarpat, mangalashtak and akshata (P12); the Tamil 'thali' joke (P4). The script strings I could check are correct. But ten languages is a huge error surface; P11's 'mangalam at every wedding' is unverified; and 'mangal' sits next to Mangal dosha ('Manglik') and the folk belief that Tuesday is a poor day for some purchases. | voice/caption quality 9: the funniest, most Indian lines in any proposal ('Rhodium is a metal. We checked.', 'Good luck to whoever has to return it next.', 'tell her the envelope was the trailer', 'in 2040 it will hold safety pins'); offer line only in P4 and P10. | premium execution risk 5: about 13 typefaces; keyline and offset on Velista; sunburst, side garlands, ribbon and chaabi on P1; a drawn object on every tile. A single Indic shaping error kills the premium read. | restraint vs clutter 5: P1 is the busiest tile of all four options. Every tile stacks a top-left wordmark, eyebrow, setup line, headline, drawn object, piece, price label, seal (tulip + MANGAL + script + chaabi) and grain. | legal risk 8: claims stay safe; the P9 customer photo is gated on her written yes; no third-party marks; sacred symbols avoided. 'Tuesday gold' could be read as a gold-content claim in Dhanteras week. | consistency 8: one seal, a rotating script, House Rule N° 01-10 and a Tuesday column make a strong system. | wordmark/type rules 5: it adds seven Tiro families, Noto Serif Gujarati and Malayalam, Gulzar and Kalam to a three-face house, and distorts Velista with strokes and offsets. The wordmark-once rule is respected.
best_posts: P3 'NOT LOCKER GOLD. TUESDAY GOLD.': the owner's 10/10 line staged in the steel almirah, with a funny locker list ('naphthalene, for reasons', 'one coin every dhanteras'). Needs the tone bracket on the cover.
P6 'THE DABBA NEVER GOES BACK EMPTY.': the Maharashtrian faral ritual, 'Mrs. Joshi, B-204', ruby huggies; all four colours on slide 3.
P8 'ONE RING: I'VE REACHED. TWO RINGS: CALL ME BACK.': a pair of huggies is literally two rings. The best reel concept of the four.
P12 'SHUBH MANGAL. SAAVDHAN.': the most culturally exact Marathi wedding tile in any option (antarpat, akshata).
P5 rangoli Prism: 'Dhanteras asks for something new and something metal. Rhodium is a metal. We checked.'
weakest_posts: P1 key art: marigold ground, sunburst, side tulip garlands, nine scripts with keylines and misregistration, ribbon, tulips and chaabi. Maximal clutter as the first post after 76 days.
P4 Mangal Thali: 7 slides, 5 pieces, a block-print buti behind a drawn thali; dense.
P10 Shaadi Calendar: 8 slides, 6 pieces, a printed November calendar with circled dates; the third multi-piece guide.
P11: the owner's favourite clean plate, reused and then covered with a headline, a price label and the seal.
fatal_or_must_fix: P3 cover: add '[ 18K GOLD TONE PLATED ]' on slide 1 next to 'TUESDAY GOLD.'. Never let the gold idiom appear without the tone bracket in the same frame.

P1: strip the sunburst and side garlands; move off the full marigold ground (lilac or blush, marigold as the ink accent the ad system allows); show at most four or five scripts on the cover and keep the full table on slide 2.
Every Indic string in ten languages needs a native reader before rendering. Drop any language that cannot be verified. Never let copy or comment replies drift to 'Manglik'.
P6 s2 'ONE ROW OF RUBY.': add 'ruby-red cubic zirconia' on the slide.
Keep the MANGAL seal and tulip bracket off the owner's clean approved plates (P5, P11); a Jost label is enough there.
Check the four AI-generated plates (P3 perf-ads woven-gold-hoops-worn, P5 P01_a1, P7 H09_a1, P11 approved plate 07) against the listing photos: braid, stone order, claws, scale.
Swap one of the two mithai beats (P6 drawn kaju katli, P7 kaju katli photo); food props are on her dislike list.
The extra typefaces (Tiro family, Noto, Gulzar, Kalam) need the owner's sign-off.
graftable_ideas: 'Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.' as one thesis tile, with the tone bracket.
The dabba-never-goes-back-empty Diwali tile.
The missed-call reel for huggies.
The 'good box is never thrown away' packaging reel (COD and insured shipping said calmly).
'Rhodium is a metal. We checked.' for any Dhanteras rhodium post.
'Shubh mangal saavdhan' antarpat finale for the Maharashtra-heavy audience.
Honest 'it arrives after the moon' delivery lines.
One rotating script word per tile instead of nine at once.

scores.proposal: proposal-retro-print.json · FLOWER BRAND · The Naira Reissue (पुनर्मुद्रण)
scores.criteria: brand fit 6: Naira inks and Velista, but no cover carries the NAIRA wordmark (only a 22 px Jost slug). A new 'FLOWER BRAND' trade-mark seal turns the flower from a 6-15% ghost into a solid emblem on all 12 covers, a sub-brand the house never had, and vintage print pastiche is a generic D2C nostalgia register. | owner-taste fit 6: nostalgia told with love (P7 inland letter, P9 'Name: Mummy', P3 earring card) and lilac, oxblood and plum. Against it: TV colour bars (P1); a Sivakasi cracker label with sunburst, star border and 'DIWALI SPECIAL' ribbon (P6); a stamp and postmark (P10), the kind she stripped from Colour Camps; and an apricot ground (P7) edging toward tan. | truthfulness 6: listing facts are mostly exact and scale is disclosed ('SHOWN LARGER THAN IT IS'). But alt text claims 'a real gold tennis bracelet' (P6) and 'a real braided gold hoop' (P3), with bare 'gold' in the P1, P2, P7 and P11 alt text. P8's cover handwriting reads 'gold & rhodium'. 'Waterproof and tarnish free' is printed on images in 8 of 12 posts (P2, P3, P5, P6, P7, P10, P11, P12), including Edition Two pieces (P5, P6, P11, P12), although an earlier owner rule bars water claims on Edition Two and the site FAQ says remove pieces before swimming. The Bold Nocturne Bracelet's pavé link (P12) conflicts with the listing text. | cultural accuracy 8: the DD slate phrase is spelled right; 'chand nikla' on the terrace; the fancy-store earring card; the inland letter's 'no enclosures'; June notebook labels; Nashik Road's stamp press (true, wording to verify); the Marathi calendar with articles on the back. The kids' card line uses 'mausi' where the idiom is usually 'mama' (fine). A firecracker on Diwali day in a pollution-ban year is a sensitivity. | voice/caption quality 8: 'No enclosures. he enclosed one anyway.', 'NAME Mummy / SUBJECT Herself, for once', 'EXACT CONTENTS: 1', 'normal programming resumes, in four colours.'; offer line in 7 of 12 captions. | premium execution risk 5: twelve bespoke vintage formats each need high SVG craft on top of halftone, misregistration and paper scan. P1's bars and P6's cracker label are costume risks. P4's cover headline is 72 px, under the 90 px grid-read rule. | restraint vs clutter 6: one idiom per tile, but some idioms are busy by nature (P6, P1, and P12's calendar with ten scribbles). | legal risk 6: misleading-claim exposure from the 'real gold' alt text and blanket waterproof lines; a postage-stamp lookalike (P10) and a public-broadcaster slate (P1) are low but real risks; the firecracker. | consistency 7: slug, seal and colophon are consistent, but the grid reads as twelve different objects held together only by ink. | wordmark/type rules 6: the wordmark is off every cover; the flower rule changes; Kalam is added; misregistration falls on four Velista titles.
best_posts: P7 'NO ENCLOSURES. he enclosed one anyway.': the Bhai Dooj inland letter from a brother; Heartbead correctly rhodium; warm and specific.
P9 'NAME Mummy / STD. Every one, twice / SUBJECT Herself, for once': Children's Day turned to the real buyer; Ribbon Bead ₹799.
P3 'DO CHOTI' fancy-store earring card: Woven Gold Hoops pinned through lilac board, '(for the other ear.)'.
P4 'IT WAS ALWAYS A MATCHBOX.': the blush drawer box as product; 'EXACT CONTENTS: 1'.
P10 Nashik stamp: Prism Rivière as 'three colours, not seven'; home-city pride.
weakest_posts: P6 Anar cracker box: loud marigold label, 'DIWALI SPECIAL' banner (reads as a sale), firecracker sensitivity, and 'real gold tennis bracelet' in the alt text.
P1 Doordarshan colour bars: the most garish possible opener, and the brand name is unreadable in the grid.
P12 December calendar: dense scribbles; the bracelet listing conflict.
P5 mithai lid: food wit over four pieces, a waterproof line on Edition Two pieces, 'Emerald' used as a cuff name beside 'pista barfi'.
fatal_or_must_fix: Alt text: P6 'a real gold tennis bracelet' and P3 'a real braided gold hoop' become 'gold-tone'. Sweep the P1, P2, P7 and P11 alt text for bare 'gold' too. As written, this is a gold-content claim.

Take 'Waterproof and tarnish free' off the image colophons, at minimum for Edition Two pieces (P5, P6, P11, P12), and remove P6's 'Waterproof and tarnish free. Light it every evening.' If water must be mentioned, use Matching Centre P5's 'listed as waterproof … we'd still take them off to swim'.
P8 tape-label handwriting 'gold & rhodium' becomes 'gold tone & rhodium'.
Put NAIRA (wordmark) or NAIRA PETITE at grid-readable size on the covers. The FLOWER BRAND seal breaks the 6-15% ghost rule and invents a sub-brand: owner sign-off or drop it.
P6: drop the 'DIWALI SPECIAL' ribbon and the star border. P12: resolve the Bold Nocturne Bracelet's construction before claiming 'one set in pavé'.
P10: verify the India Security Press, Nashik Road wording; keep the stamp unmistakably non-official (no value, no emblem, as specified).
graftable_ideas: The P7 inland-letter Bhai Dooj tile ('no enclosures').
The P9 'Name: Mummy' notebook label for Children's Day.
P4's matchbox as the blush drawer box: packaging as product.
'Nashik Road prints the country's stamps' as a home-pride line for Prism.
The THE ORIGINAL / THE REISSUE / THE PIECE colophon as a carousel closer.
'Sorry for the interruption' as a one-line acknowledgement of the 11-week silence.

recommendation: Through the brand-and-truth lens the ranking is Matching Centre 81, The Fitting Book 78, MANGAL 69, Retro Reissue 64. Show Matching Centre as Option A once its P2 is fixed: wrong stone cut, wrong sizing claim, and a fixed-size ring offered as a Karwa Chauth gift. The cleanest swap is Couture's size-free Silk Mesh Cuff, or the adjustable Verdant Eternity Band. Also fix the P8 'choker' and confirm the WhatsApp matching service. For Option B, The Fitting Book is the safest brand pick, but it shares Matching Centre's world (pinked swatches, tailor's tape, order slips, the couture-house argument), so the owner would be choosing between two versions of one idea. If the two options must differ in kind, as the owner's PTAT ask implies, pair Matching Centre with MANGAL, and only after MANGAL's must-fixes: strip P1 (no sunburst or garlands, no full marigold ground, four or five scripts on the cover), put the tone bracket on P3's 'TUESDAY GOLD.' cover, have a native reader check every Indic string, keep the seal off the clean approved plates, and swap one of the two kaju katli beats. MANGAL has the strongest owner-sourced wit and the most PTAT-like system; its weakness is execution density, not truth. Retro should not be shown as written: its claims hygiene ('real gold' alt text, waterproof printed on Edition Two pieces) and the invented FLOWER BRAND sub-brand fail this lens. Its P7 inland letter and P9 'Name: Mummy' graft cleanly into MANGAL's nostalgia lane. The Fitting Book's P3 neckline guide, P11 dupatta guide and P6 '25 MM.' graft cleanly into Matching Centre, for example in place of P9 '36 CM.'. Across every option: re-read Ruby variant stock (12 today) on each posting morning, and keep water claims off images except in Matching P5's 'listed as … we'd still take them off' form.
